body.statement: Suppose \(q_x>0\) for both \(x\in B\).  At the level of the joint law \(P\) and unconditional APE \(\Delta\), the weak legal parameterization by one unconditional probability law \(\mu\), initial kernel \(h\), and unrestricted feedback kernel \(g\) is exactly equivalent to this note's measure-valued conditional reformulation of the Bonhomme--Dano--Graham two-period equations.  The forward map normalizes the finite measure \(h_xd\mu\) by \(q_x\); the reverse map takes the \(q_x\)-weighted mixture of the two conditional probability laws and recovers \(h_x\) by a Radon--Nikodym derivative.  The reformulation permits arbitrary probability measures on \((0,\infty)\), including atomic, absolutely continuous, and mixed laws.  The strict class \(\mathcal M_+(c)\) is an additional subclass of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\).  Neither direction establishes equality with the published fixed-reference or Lebesgue-density program.
body.proof_tex:
Let \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\) generate \(P\).  Summing its sequential path law over \((y,z,w)\), using successively \(\sum_{w\in B}p_z(w,u)=1\), \(\sum_{z\in B}g_{xy}(z,u)=1\), and \(\sum_{y\in B}p_x(y,u)=1\), gives
\[
 q_x=\sum_{y,z,w\in B}P(x,y,z,w)=\int h_x(u)\,d\mu(u). \tag{1}
\]
Because \(q_x>0\), define, for each Borel set \(E\subset(0,\infty)\),
\[
 \pi_x(E)=q_x^{-1}\int_E h_x(u)\,d\mu(u). \tag{2}
\]
Equation (1) makes \(\pi_x\) a probability measure.  The history-conditioned response factorization and feedback normalization then give
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)
 =q_x\int p_x(y,u)g_{xy}(z,u)p_z(w,u)\,d\pi_x(u), \tag{3}
\]
and, on putting \(f_c(u)=(c-1)u/\{(1+u)(1+cu)\}\),
\[
 \Delta
 =\sum_{x\in B}q_x\int f_c(u)\,d\pi_x(u). \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, (4) follows from \(d\mu=\sum_xh_xd\mu=\sum_xq_xd\pi_x\).  Equations (3)--(4) define the note's measure-valued conditional reformulation of the two-period path and APE equations.  The source scope of the corresponding published program is recorded separately in \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\).

Conversely, let \(q_0,q_1>0\) sum to one, let \(\pi_0,\pi_1\) be probability measures on \((0,\infty)\), and let \(g\) be a measurable nonnegative feedback kernel satisfying \(\sum_{z\in B}g_{xy}(z,u)=1\) for every \(x,y\in B\) almost everywhere under each \(\pi_x\).  Suppose (3)--(4) hold, and define
\[
 \mu=\sum_{x\in B}q_x\pi_x. \tag{5}
\]
This is a probability measure, and each finite measure \(q_x\pi_x\) is dominated by \(\mu\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}radon\text{-}nikodym\text{-}finite\text{-}family}\), there are measurable versions
\[
 h_x=\frac{d(q_x\pi_x)}{d\mu},
 \qquad h_x\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_{x\in B}h_x=1
 \quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}. \tag{6}
\]
Because \(q_x\pi_x\ll\mu\), a property holding \(\pi_x\)-almost everywhere also holds on the set where \(h_x>0\), up to a \(\mu\)-null set.  On the complementary histories where \(h_x=0\), redefine \(g_{xy}(\cdot,u)\), if necessary, to any probability vector on \(B\).  Then the feedback normalization holds \(\mu\)-almost everywhere for every \(x,y\), without changing (3).  Together with the stipulated history-conditioned logit response kernels, (5)--(6) satisfy the four conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\).  Since
\[
 h_xd\mu=q_xd\pi_x, \tag{7}
\]
substitution in the sequential legal-model formula recovers (3), hence every cell of \(P\), and summing (7) over \(x\) recovers (4), hence \(\Delta\).  Thus the two maps are inverse at the level of the observable law and target.

The operations (2) and (5)--(7) preserve atomic and singular components, so they prove an unrestricted-measure correspondence on \((0,\infty)\), not an absolutely-continuous replacement theorem.  Finally, the strict legal class satisfies all weak conditions plus strict initial and feedback positivity by its definition, and therefore \(\mathcal M_+(c)\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\).  This proves the subclass and density-scope assertions.
body.justification: Conditionalization and Radon--Nikodym mixing prove equivalence with the note's measure-valued conditional reformulation.
body.gap: The maps preserve atoms and singular components and prove no equality with a fixed-reference or Lebesgue-density program.
